newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: A dearth of fresh market-moving news coupled with a general lack of interest brought activity on South Africa's rand and bond markets to a virtual standstill on Monday.
And dealers said the current lethargy in the markets looked set to continue all week and possibly until the budget on March 12.
After trading n a 4.4060 to 4.4240 range against the dollar on the day, the currency settled at 4.4135/4165 at the 1400 GMT local close.
Dealers said what little volumes they had seen came mainly in the morning session as local importer demand was met by offshore investment house and local exporter dollar selling.
The afternoon session was characterised by thin volume, orderly, two-way trade, they said.
"It's been a difficult day for most people I think," a currency trader said. "The rand has been looking for a range but it doesn't look like it wants to go anywhere."
A market holiday in the U.S. was also cited as a reason for the low level of activity through the day.
The rand did manage to make some progress against the crosses as the dollar continued its resurgence against other international currencies.
The local unit was last quoted at 7.1468/1547 against sterling from 7.1602/1695 on Friday and at 0.3840/3844 marks from 0.3814/3818 marks previously.
On the bond market, trade was equally lugubrious as the market consolidated its recent gains and most players kept to the sidelines.
"It has basically been a non-event day," a trader said.
The key R150 was last pegged at 14.715 percent from 14.735 percent on Friday.
"All the good new3 is in the price and we are looking for a bit of sideways movement this week," the trader said.

Traders said that while there was concern about the money market shortage remaining above the 10 billion rand mark, it had done little to dent sentiment which has helped carry long bond yields almost 150 points lower since the begining of the year.

The Reserve Bank's assistant general manager of money and capital markets Roelf du Plooy said the shortage, which rose to 10.453 billion rand on Saturday from 10.139 billion rand on Friday, appeared to be a result of foreign exchange outflows.
Money market rates were unmoved by the continuing squeeze on liquidity, holding steady at their overnight levels.
Three-month NCDs were quoted at between 16.40 offered and 16.65 percent bid and the 90-day BA rate at between 15.80 and 16.05 percent.

Bond traders said they expected yields to move in a 10-point band during the week and possibly up until budget day, barring any major announcements by Finance Minister Tretor Manuel and Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals at two meetings this week.
The two will address an investment conference on Tuesday before briefing bond market investors on Thursday.
Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners were net buyers of 492.54 million rands worth of South African bonds on Friday after selling 20.84 million rands on Thursday.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 12.12 billion rand on Friday from 43.66 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement date.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
